core.title: Declare each user/system flow's family (behavior or delivery) to match its terminal contract
core.given: A user/system flow definition (a plan artifact) exists or is being written: it is authored, edited (family, terminal contract or user/system flow ID added, changed or removed), or reviewed/validated even if unchanged.
core.when: The planner sets, adds or corrects a user/system flow's family; adds, changes or removes its terminal contract; proposes or changes a user/system flow ID; or reviews/validates existing user/system flow definitions.
core.then: Declare family as delivery if and only if the declared terminal contract requires a durable Acceptance Authority commit and terminates in the acceptance-commit receipt (the profile's commit-receipt URN); otherwise declare behavior.
prefer: Derive family from the terminal contract (the source of truth); family is its validator-checked assertion, so re-derive it whenever the terminal contract changes.
behavior: observe, exercise, classify, validate, recommend or report a capability against a system under examination; no authority commit.
delivery: govern accepted-system state through a durable Acceptance Authority commit.
avoid: Encoding family in the user/system flow ID (never an ID digit).
Omitting family (mandatory) or treating it as a second source of truth that diverges from the terminal contract.
Inferring family from the variant category (values 0-3) or vice versa; the axes are orthogonal.
core.why: Behavior user/system flows only exercise a capability; delivery user/system flows change accepted-system state via an authority commit. Deriving family from the terminal contract keeps this checkable and out of IDs and variant categories.
evidence: The family check passes: every user/system flow's family equals the family derived from its declared terminal contract.
Every user/system flow definition has a family field with value behavior or delivery.
No user/system flow ID encodes the family.
verification: Derivation: a terminal contract that requires a durable Acceptance Authority commit AND terminates in the profile's commit-receipt URN => delivery; any other terminal contract => behavior.

Allowed family values: behavior | delivery; family is mandatory on every user/system flow definition. The concrete user/system-flow-definition field layout in which the family field lives is supplied by the profile's plan-syntax user/system-flow-schema entry, not fixed here.

Missing family, or a family that mismatches the family derived from the declared terminal contract, is a finding; the check runs on all user/system flow definitions, not only changed ones, so unchanged definitions under review or validation can fail it.

Not covered: the check does not cross-check family against the variant-category axis (values 0-3; the two axes are orthogonal), and it does not itself verify that user/system flow IDs omit the family (kept in avoid; an independent obligation is suggested for it).

values: user/system flow family missing or mismatching the family derived from its terminal contract

fires: A planner authors a new user/system flow definition and must set its family.
A planner adds, changes or removes a user/system flow's terminal contract (for example to or away from one returning the acceptance-commit receipt), even without touching family.
A planner corrects an existing user/system flow's family value, or adds a missing family field, without changing the terminal contract.
A planner reviews or validates existing user/system flow definitions that were not edited, and must check each family is present and matches its terminal contract.
A planner proposes or changes user/system flow IDs, including a scheme that encodes behavior/delivery as a digit.
doesNotFire: Choosing only the variant category (0-3) of a user/system flow without touching, reviewing or validating family, terminal contract or user/system flow ID.
Editing product capability or DESIRED OUTCOME (plan-artifact) content that does not change, review or validate any user/system flow's terminal contract, family or ID.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds of the stack, so the file_kind fact and the check can recognize user/system flow definitions as plan artifacts.

The concrete field layout of a user/system flow definition in the stack's plan syntax (where the mandatory family field lives), so a check can locate and read family on every user/system flow definition.
The URN of the Acceptance Authority's commit receipt that a delivery user/system flow's terminal contract terminates in; the derivation of family = delivery depends on it.

neutralityNotes: User/system flow, family, terminal contract, Acceptance Authority, variant category (including its method-level 0-3 value range), product capability and DESIRED OUTCOME are ATDD-method concepts (user-system-flow/desired-outcome/capability appear in the closed vocabulary's artifact params) and remain in the core. The concrete stack-representation data the core needs all come from the profile as entries of v3 map keys, so no key is proposed: the commit-receipt URN via urn.grammar#commit_receipt, and the user/system-flow-definition schema shape via idiom.plan_syntax#user_system_flow_schema (the field layout itself is no longer stated in core verification; the core keeps only the mandatory family assertion and the behavior/delivery value set). Realization details kept in bunOnly: the validator/finding id planner.user-system-flow.family-matches-terminal-contract and the sibling rule id planner.user-system-flow.categories. The concrete receipt-URN example inside fires[1] was neutralized to 'the acceptance-commit receipt' (bun.json itself ships as the reference example). unless is empty in the realization and stays empty in the core. No per-rule severity or disposition is declared in bun.json, so none was added.
